correctness.rationale: The first-run identity follows by inspecting the decreasing-priority vertices of one color and checking cross-part adjacency. Independent colorwise relative rankings give conditional product laws. The binomial beta integral proves the exact expectation. Under k_n log n=o(n), simultaneous Chernoff concentration makes all per-color part fractions uniformly close to their limiting values and yields uniformly geometric-tailed independent run variables; conditional Berry–Esseen gives the Gaussian. A Hamming-Lipschitz extension of the conditional mean plus Efron–Stein bounds its fluctuations by O(k^2/n)=o(k), and total variance yields the variance limit. Actual package checker exhaustively confirms 1254 conditional finite laws and further exact identities, without claiming to prove the infinite limit.

The 2026 motivating paper supplies the peak equivalence and a two-part fixed-palette limit (credited); the 1989 full-text example addresses unlabeled local maxima on a regular graph without iid color splitting. value.rationale: Dense complete multipartite community graphs are natural graphs for randomized one-at-a-time correction. The finite law factorizes into hypergeometric initial runs, and the color count forces a real change from fixed-k non-Gaussian geometric-mixture totals to a triangular Gaussian limit with explicit variance. This is a distributional regime difference not supplied by a simple computation of a textbook mean. The result does not claim optimal growth thresholds or generic graph universality.
